title: Global market: Eurozone bond yields steady as oil prices ease, traders assess Iran sanctions
description: Eurozone bond yields remained largely stable as investors assessed new U.S. sanctions on Iran and easing oil prices. Germany’s 10-year yield held near a 15-year high, while longer-term yields stayed elevated amid inflation risks, energy costs and fiscal spending. Stronger German growth reinforced expectations for ECB rate hikes, keeping borrowing costs high across Europe.

title: Conflict-hit oil supply crisis deepens as nearly half of global output comes from affected countries
description: Nearly half of the world’s oil supply now comes from countries affected by conflict, highlighting the growing vulnerability of global energy markets. Reuters calculations based on IEA data show that Iran, Russia, Ukraine, Libya and Venezuela produced around 45 million barrels per day in 2025, accounting for more than 43% of global oil supply.

title: 697 days, no new record high: Sensex hits worst two-year return stretch since 2012. Will this end soon?
description: The Sensex has gone 697 days without a new record high, marking its longest stretch of weakness in years. In 2026, 37% of trading days have delivered negative two-year returns, the highest share since 2012. However, easing FII selling, resilient domestic flows and potential foreign inflows could support a recovery.

title: NSE IPO coming soon: Should investors buy unlisted shares now or wait for the mega issue?
description: With NSE’s IPO expected in the second half of September, investors face a choice between buying its unlisted shares or waiting for the public issue. NSE’s unlisted shares are currently trading around Rs 2,015, little changed from their level when the exchange filed its DRHP. The stock has traded between Rs 1,800 and Rs 2,150 over the past year.

title: Q1 earnings show resilience, but downside risks still loom. HSBC explains why
description: Indian companies delivered better-than-expected Q1FY27 earnings, with around 70% of firms meeting or beating HSBC’s estimates. Mid- and small-cap companies led growth, while financials drove earnings upgrades. However, HSBC flagged risks of downgrades in coming quarters as elevated commodity prices persist and the benefits of GST cuts and inventory gains fade.

title: Bernstein cuts PFC, REC target prices as bank competition weighs on loan growth
description: Bernstein has retained an Outperform rating on Power Finance Corporation (PFC) and REC but cut its target prices and loan-growth estimates, citing stronger competition from banks, slower renewable capacity additions and improving financial health among state-owned DISCOMs. The brokerage lowered its target to Rs 465 for PFC and Rs 410 for REC, while reducing FY26-FY28 loan-book growth estimates to 7%.

title: IIFL Finance shares drop 8% as IIFL Home Finance gets Rs 963 crore tax demand

The company disputed the additions and said it is pursuing appellate remedies. Separately, IIFL Finance secured a stay on a Rs 475.56 crore tax demand.

title: Jackson Hole 2026: When and what are investors expecting from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh?
description: The Federal Reserve’s Jackson Hole symposium, scheduled for August 27-29, will draw close attention as Chair Kevin Warsh makes his expected debut. Investors seek signals on inflation and interest-rate policy amid bond-market jitters. With inflation above target, markets anticipate potentially higher rates, while President Trump continues pressing the Fed for cuts.

title: India bonds flat as oil prices shrug off US curbs on Iran
description: Indian government bonds experienced little movement early Tuesday, stabilizing after a recent decline. Oil prices reacted unfazed to new US sanctions, which alleviated some importer tensions. Market players are anticipating an upcoming state debt sale that could reveal investor appetite. Although bond yields are stable, lingering inflation and currency effects might weaken the market's mood. Nevertheless, abundant banking liquidity continues to bolster demand for bonds.
